analysis.title: Delta-One Flows & Positioning: Equity ETF inflows hit multiyear highs, but CIBs/model rebalances skew the signal and futures lag; levered Semis de-gross; Fixed Income soft
key_insights: US-listed equity ETFs drew $74.6Bn in the week (2.7z), the strongest inflows in at least 5 years, led by the US ($65Bn, 2.7z). JPM estimates about 20% of US inflows came from CIB-related creations that may reverse this week. Underlying inflows stayed strong even excluding them.

Equity futures flows were weak (-1.6z) with heavy selling in MSCI EM (-3.8z). Large net selling (below -1.5z) also showed in MID, DAX, Germany 5y/10y and SOFR. Large net buying (above 1.5z) showed in AUD futures.

Fixed income flows were weak in both futures (-1.7z) and ETFs (-2z). Treasury ETFs saw $4.2Bn of outflows (-3.1z) as a large issuer model rebalance cut broad and short-term Treasury exposure, with only part reallocated to long-term bonds.

Tech flows were mixed. QQQ led ETF inflows (+$11.3Bn) and investors bought SMH (+$1.9Bn) and NVDL (+$0.7Bn). Levered semis ETFs saw $5.5Bn of net outflows across SOXL (-$3.7Bn) and SOXS (-$1.8Bn). Tech sector ETFs overall posted -$2Bn (-0.8z).
NVDL attracted about $0.7Bn as investors bought the dip after NVDA's recent underperformance, against the trend of levered product outflows (-$5.2Bn, -2.2z).
Defensive sectors led ETF inflows, with Real Estate (3.4z) and Staples (2z). Utilities posted outflows.

Style ETF flows were distorted by CIBs and a large issuer model rebalance. Quality drew $4.5Bn (3.8z), led by $3.5Bn into QLTY as the fund passed its 3Y anniversary. Multifactor (4.4z) and Growth (1.5z) inflows appear CIB-driven.
Thematic ETFs saw inflows (2.5z) driven by model-rebalance demand for THRO and likely CIB-related buying across ARK funds, which may reverse this week.

CTAs likely remain neutral to short US equities, with SPX/NDX/RTY all trading about 3-4% below key momentum signals that could trigger releveraging. They likely sold long-term USTs as yields surged after last week's hot CPI print, and added to shorts in precious metals and crypto.
CTAs likely remain long European equities, short APAC (ex-Australia and India), short global rates (ex-China and Korea), short Energy (ex-natgas) and long USD vs global FX.

CFTC positioning: Asset Managers sold EAFE, covered VIX shorts (+2.8z) and added to UST 10y futures. Leveraged Funds cut SPX shorts, flipped long EAFE (+2.3z) and sold USTs. Managed Money sold oil and bought gold.
Crypto ETFs saw another week of outflows (-$1.6Bn, -1.3z), and BTC and ETH futures fell 8.0% and 8.6% on the week with CTAs short.
Munis saw their first outflows in nine weeks (-$0.8Bn, -1.5z). Investors rotated out of HY (-0.8z) and into IG (1z).

sector_views.rationale: Real Estate ETFs drew the strongest sector inflows at 3.4z ($1.48Bn) over the week. This is a flow reading, not a bank rating.
Staples ETFs drew inflows of 2.0z ($0.7Bn) as defensive sectors led. This is a flow reading, not a bank rating.
Tech ETFs saw $2.0Bn of outflows (-0.8z) on the week, driven by levered semis products, while QQQ and SMH drew inflows. The 4-week flow is +$12.9Bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The report says yields surged after last week's hot CPI print and CTAs likely sold long-term USTs. No CPI figure is given.

crypto_views: Crypto ETFs saw $1.6Bn of outflows on the week (-1.3z) and $3.9Bn over 4 weeks (-1.4z).
BTC futures fell 8.0% on the week to 65,115 and ETH futures fell 8.6% to 1,824. CTA signal on BTC is Neutral, down from Short a week earlier on the signal table, and ETH is Short.
CTAs added to crypto shorts week over week.
CFTC non-commercial BTC positioning was +2,230 contracts (0.3z) and ETH +1,189 (-1.7z) as of 11/10.
risk_factors: About 20% of US equity ETF inflows came from CIB-related creations that may reverse this week, so the headline inflow overstates underlying demand.
Style and thematic ETF flows, including ARK funds, are distorted by CIBs and a large issuer model rebalance and may reverse.
Equity futures flows lag the ETF inflow signal, with heavy EM selling.
CTAs sit 3-4% below US equity momentum triggers and could add to selling if levels weaken further, or re-lever if they recover.
charts_described: 4w US ETF Flows chart: equities inflows of 23.5, 35.4, 41.6 and 74.6 $Bn for the weeks ending 10/23, 10/30, 11/6 and 11/13, versus fixed income 15.2, 10.4, 14.1 and 2.1.
vol_and_positioning: VIX futures traded at 22.80, up from 18.33 a month ago, with a 1w return of -24.7% in futures flow data. CTA signal on VIX is Long.
Asset Managers covered VIX shorts (+2.8z) in the CFTC data. Non-commercial VIX w/w change was +30,759 contracts (2.7z).
SPX, NDX and RTY trade about 3-4% below key CTA momentum signals that could trigger releveraging. SPX futures are at 7,442 against a 50d MA of 7,704. NDX is at 27,350, with a Short signal.
Levered semis ETFs de-grossed: SOXL -$3.7Bn and SOXS -$1.8Bn on the week, and SOXS -$3.6Bn over 4 weeks.
VXX and VIXY were the top 4-week performers at +28.5% and +28.2%, and the bottom 1-week performers at -14.7%.
Yield-income single-stock option ETFs diverged: AMDY led 1-week gains at +17.2% while MSTY (-13.4%) and NVDY (-13.2%) were among the weakest.
